projectDesc.p: Encoded for the Experiencing War web site for the Veterans History Project.

samplingDecl.p: The recording of the interview with Jacob B. Armstrong was digitized.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was encoded with minimal changes to the original text in an effort to preserve original content and idiosyncrasies of the person interviewed. Period language and terminology are also retained. Encoding is literal with regard to the transcriptionist's capitalization, punctuation, and spelling. Spelling errors are indicated with [sic]; however, recurring errors in spelling within a single document have been marked the first time and not subsequently.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: This is April 10th, 2003, at my grandma's house in Evansville, Indiana. My name is Carrie Schindler, and I am interviewing J. B. Armstrong. Okay. What branch of service did you serve in?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: I served in the Air Force.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: And what war was it?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: In World War II and then in Korea.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Okay. And what was your rank?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: I was -- I was a captain, a spot promotion for a captain.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: And where did you serve?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: In Korea.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Where were you drafted, or where did you enlist?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: I was drafted in Evansville, Indiana. And I went into the infantry, but I transferred into the Air Force after I was in the infantry about six months.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Where exactly did you go during the war?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: You don't want me to name all them places?

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: Well, I went to Fort Benjamin Harrison to be inducted. And then I went to Louisiana. From there I went to Texas. From Texas I went to Hayes, Kansas to school. Then to Santa Ana, California; from there to King City, California; from there to Merced, California; from there to Phoenix, Arizona. And then I drew my overseas equipment and the war ended, and I came home.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Were there many casualties in your unit?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: What?

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Were there many casualties in your unit?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: We lost quite a few pilots; right. We got, I'd say, maybe half of them back with a helicopter. But we actually lost, oh -- I'd say we lost 25 or 30.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Tell me a couple of your most memorable experiences.

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: Well, the funniest one, we had two airplanes going to escort a flying boat up to the mouth of the Chung Chung River to get a F-84 boy out that had been shot down. Only trouble was when we got there, there was two of them in one little one-man dinghy. And the dumbo wouldn't land because there was ground fire shooting at these two guys from the post. And we were to eliminate them so the dumbo could land and get the two pilots.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Were you awarded any medals or citations?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: I got the Korean War Medal. I got the Service Ribbon for the United States for Korea. And I got the Distinguished Flying Cross. And I got -- I don't know, another one. I don't remember now what it was.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: How did you stay in touch with your family?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: What?

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: How did you stay in touch with your family?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: Well, every five weeks while I was in Korea, we would have five days off and we would go to Japan and I would call home. And then we wore the mail boxes out. (Laughter.)

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: What was the food like over there?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: The what?

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: The food. What was it like?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: We had very good food, the best I ever had anyplace in the Air Force.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Did you feel pressure or stress?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: Did I feel what?

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Pressure or stress.

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: Oh, no. Not bad. We'd get scared sometimes, but that's acceptable. (Laughter.)

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Was there something special you did for good luck?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: No. I just hoped.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Where all did you travel during your service?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: Well, I traveled all over California. Then went to Florida. I went to Hawaii, then to Wake Island, and to Japan. We spent quite a bit of time in Japan because every five weeks why we would go there for five days. And then on into Korea.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Were there any entertainers that you had?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: Who did I tell you? MRS.

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: Betty Hudson.

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: Who? MRS.

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: Betty Hudson.

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: Oh, yeah. Betty Hudson troupe come over and entertained us. There was about, I don't know, about five or six people in our group and they had a very good show.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Do you recall any particular humorous or unusual event?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: Unusual?

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: What?

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Something funny that happened, an event.

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: Well, the funniest thing that happened was that mission I was telling you about was Ray and I escorting that dumbo. They was shooting at this one-man dinghy out there in the water, and we were shooting at the guys in the gunning placement on the coast. I had a drop tank that would not feed. And so I still had it hung under my wing. And I got the bright idea that I was going to drop that in that gunning placement. And that's exactly where it went. (Laughter.)

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: What did you think of officers or fellow soldiers?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: Oh, I -- they were good guys, really. Even our commanding general was only 38 years old.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Did you keep a personal diary or anything?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: No, I didn't.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: You didn't? Oh. Do you recall the day your service ended?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: Recall what?

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: The day your service ended.

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: The 1st of October of '55.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Where were you?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: I was at home in the Reserve.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: What did you do in the days and weeks afterward?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: After I came home?

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: I went to work, back to work to the railroad. I worked for the railroad before I left.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Did you make a lot of close friendships while in the service?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: I made about three or four very close friends. Sattenstein (ph) lived in New York, but we corresponded a long time. A guy named Zelliott (ph), I got his picture here somewhere. I made a good friendship with him. He lived up in Iowa. And a couple other guys. One in Louisville.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Did you join any Veterans organizations?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: I belong to the VFW, and to the American Legion.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: What did you go on to do as a career after the war?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: I was an engineer on a locomotive for the CSX Railroad.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: How did your service and experience affect your life?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: Well, not really bad. Just being gone; that's all.

sp.speaker: Carrie Schindler
sp.p: Is there anything you'd like to add? Any stories, or anything else you'd like to tell?

sp.speaker: Jacob B. Armstrong
sp.p: Well, a fellow named Tommy got hit and had to bail out on my very first mission. And I thought, of course, they're not very good if they're all like this. (Laughter.)
[END OF INTERVIEW]
